rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited commands illustrate the Qur’an’s varied use of obedience language; a plural may address a collective body or distribute a ruling across its individual members.
rows.anchor: الموارد المختلفة بالإثبات والنفي والإخبار والإنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plural used for one of its individual members differs from a ruling addressed to a plural distributively, as in commanding each scholar separately.
rows.anchor: أن يطلق لفظ الجمع ويراد به واحد من آحاده لا أن يوقع حكم على الجمع

rows.speaker: المنار
rows.claim: One proposed reading takes Uli al-amr collectively as trusted people of influence, including scholars, military and public-interest leaders, labor and party heads, and newspaper editors.
rows.anchor: كما ذكره في المنار هم أهل الحل والعقد الذين تثق بهم الأمة من العلماء والرؤساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This collective reading faces the problem that the verse entails infallibility, a consequence its proponents among the commentators accept.
rows.anchor: الآية دالة - كما عرفت - على عصمة أولي الأمر وقد اضطر إلى قبول ذلك القائلون بهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The members of a collective council cannot each be infallible, since no such council has ever assembled and it is inconceivable that God command what has no real instance.
rows.anchor: من البديهي أن لم يمر بهذه الأمة يوم يجتمع فيه جماعة من أهل الحل والعقد كلهم معصومون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infallibility cannot literally inhere in an abstract collective body whose individual members may commit idolatry or sin.
rows.anchor: وكيف يتصور اتصاف موضوع اعتباري بصفة حقيقية أعني اتصاف الهيئة الاجتماعية بالعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers a possible account in which God protects the council’s judgment from error, as a mutawātir report is protected from falsehood, without infallibility being an added attribute of its members or the body.
rows.anchor: حقيقته أن الله يصون هذه الهيئة أن تأمر بمعصية أو ترى رأيا فتخطئ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that account, the verse promises only that their judgment is sound and accords with the Book and Sunna, as divine care for the community.
rows.anchor: والآية لا تدل على أزيد من أن رأيهم غير خابط بل مصيب يوافق الكتاب والسنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says that the Prophet’s community will not agree upon error; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats its relevance conditionally, if its chain is sound.
rows.anchor: " لا تجتمع أمتي على خطأ "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if sound, the report concerns consensus of the whole community, not consensus of its decision-makers; the terms name different groups, and the report denies agreement on error rather than denying error within a consensus.
rows.anchor: إن صحت فإنما تنفي اجتماع الأمة على خطأ ولا تنفى اجتماع أهل الحل والعقد منهم على خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report instead means that error never encompasses the entire community: at least some people, perhaps one infallible person, remain on truth, preserving the religion until the end of time.
rows.anchor: أن الخطأ في مسألة من المسائل لا يستوعب الأمة بل يكون دائما فيهم من هو على الحق

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Reports transmitted through multiple routes attribute to the Prophet the prediction that Jews divide into 71 sects, Christians into 72, and Muslims into 73, all doomed except one; the author calls these reports sound.
rows.anchor: الروايات الواردة من طرق شتى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الدالة على افتراق اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The no-consensus-on-error report does not answer what would make the decision-makers’ collective judgments infallible, if they are what Uli al-amr means.
rows.anchor: وإنما الكلام في معنى عصمة أهل الحل والعقد من الأمة لو كان هو المراد بقوله وأولي الأمر منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Councils of influential people occur in every nation, clan, and community; history shows them reaching decisions that sometimes prove right and sometimes wrong.
rows.anchor: هذه العصابة التي شأنها الحل والعقد في الأمور غير مختصة بالأمة المسلمة بل كل أمة من الأمم العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Islamic councils were protected from error, that protection would require an extraordinary, miraculous cause rather than ordinary social factors.
rows.anchor: فلو كان الرأي الاجتماعي من أهل الحل والعقد في الإسلام مصونا عن الخطأ فإنما هو بعامل ليس من سنخ العوامل العادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a continuing miracle would merit Qur’anic explanation of its scope and the council’s duties, and prophetic instruction to the community and its future leaders; the text supplies none.
rows.anchor: فكان من اللازم أن يبين القرآن حدوده وسعة دائرته ويمتن الله به كما أمتن بالقرآن وبمحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community, especially the Companions, would have been expected to ask about so important a divinely granted authority; they asked about lesser matters such as lunar phases, spending, and spoils.
rows.anchor: وقد سألوا عن أشياء لا قدر لها بالنسبة إلى هذه المهمة كالأهلة وماذا ينفقون والأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No trace of the council’s infallibility appears in preserved post-Prophetic disputes and debates, although transmitters recorded them in detail.
rows.anchor: فما لهذه الحقيقة لا توجد لها عين ولا أثر في احتجاجاتهم ومناظراتهم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says a fifth interpretation violates the compound consensus because the known positions are the four caliphs, military commanders, scholars, or infallible Imams; he then says it reduces to the scholars’ view, undoing his objection.
rows.anchor: فإن الأقوال في معنى أولي الأمر لا تجاوز أربعة الخلفاء الراشدون وأمراء السرايا والعلماء والأئمة المعصومون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collective-infallibility reading appeared only among some later commentators, not the early Companions and Successors, and therefore was not understood as a special miraculous gift to the council.
rows.anchor: ولم تظهر بين قدماء المفسرين من الصحابة والتابعين حتى ذهب إليه شرذمة من المتأخرين الرازي وبعض من بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ordinary Islamic education cannot make a consensus infallible: collective cognition is the sum of individual cognition, so if each person may err, the group may err too.
rows.anchor: وهو أن إدراك الكل هو مجموع إدراكات الأبعاض وإذا جاز الخطأ على كل واحد واحد جاز على الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Post-Prophetic history records councils steering the community into error, injustice, bloodshed, and the suspension of rulings; their decisions helped cause those harms.
rows.anchor: اجتمع فيه أهل الحل والعقد من المسلمين على ما اجتمعوا عليه ثم سلكوا طريقا يهديهم إليه رأيهم فلم يزيدوا إلا ضلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Uli al-amr are fallible councils, they must be treated as ordinary people who sometimes err, though their expertise may make errors rare; obedience is then excused for the greater public benefit.
rows.anchor: نقول بجواز خطأهم وأنهم على حد سائر الناس يصيبون ويخطؤون غير أنهم لما كانوا عصابة فاضلة خبيرة بالأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This view permits the council to reinterpret or change scriptural rulings for perceived public welfare, and treats its new decisions as binding for the community’s good.
rows.anchor: فلو حكموا بما يغاير حكم الكتاب والسنة ويطابق ما شخصوه من مصلحة الأمة

rows.speaker: بعض الباحثين
rows.claim: Some researchers explicitly say that a caliph may act against plain religion to preserve the community’s welfare.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح بعض الباحثين أن الخليفة له أن يعمل بما يخالف صريح الدين حفظا لصلاح الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reduces Islam to an elected civic assembly whose laws evolve with circumstances, treating religion as a temporary social stage fitted only to the Prophet’s era and its near successors.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه أو القول - كما ترى - قول من يرى أن الدين سنة اجتماعية سبكت في قالب الدين

rows.speaker: بعض المؤلفين
rows.claim: An unnamed author says the verse establishes none of the interpretations that commentators have proposed.
rows.anchor: لا يدل على شيء مما ذكره المفسرون على اختلاف أقوالهم

rows.speaker: بعض المؤلفين
rows.claim: The author argues that obligatory obedience to Uli al-amr implies no special virtue, just as necessity can require obedience to tyrants without making them better before God.
rows.anchor: فرض طاعة أولي الأمر كائنين من كانوا لا يدل على فضل ومزية لهم على غيرهم أصلا

rows.speaker: بعض المؤلفين
rows.claim: The same author argues that the command applies only when its subject exists, like spending on a poor person or refusing to aid an oppressor, and does not require creating that subject.
rows.anchor: الحكم المذكور في الآية لا يزيد على سائر الأحكام التي تتوقف فعليتها على تحقق موضوعاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first objection wrongly assumes Uli al-amr are rulers: the Qur’an forbids obeying oppressors, profligates, and unbelievers, so it cannot explicitly join their obedience to God’s and the Messenger’s.
rows.anchor: ومن المحال أن يأمر الله مع ذلك بطاعتهم ثم يزيد على ذلك فيقرن طاعتهم بطاعة نفسه ورسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If obedience to rulers were only permitted under coercion, the Qur’an would state a permission for protective dissimulation, as it does at 3:28, rather than command obedience outright.
rows.anchor: ولو فرض كون هذه الطاعة طاعة تقية لعبر عنها بإذن ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject-contingency objection fails if Uli al-amr are divinely authorized religious leaders: they must be infallible, and a command with no or merely accidental real instance cannot anchor the community’s religious order.
rows.anchor: ومحال أن يأمر الله بطاعة من لا مصداق له أو له مصداق اتفاقي في آية تتضمن أس أساس المصالح الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The need for Uli al-amr is the community’s need for governance, comparable to its need for the Messenger; therefore the verse refers to individual infallible members whose identity God or the Prophet must designate, matching reports from the Imams of the Household.
rows.anchor: ليس إلا أن المراد بأولي الأمر آحاد من الأمة معصومون في أقوالهم مفترض طاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretations identifying Uli al-amr as the Rightly Guided Caliphs, military commanders, or scholars lack evidence, and those groups are not infallible; the author notes the exception of what one Muslim group believes about Ali.
rows.anchor: أن كلا من الأقوال الثلاث قول من غير دليل يدل عليه

rows.speaker: بعض المعترضين
rows.claim: An objection says identifying the infallible Imams requires explicit divine or prophetic explanation, otherwise no one would have disputed their identity after the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك يحتاج إلى تعريف صريح من الله ورسوله ولو كان ذلك لم يختلف في أمرهم اثنان بعد رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that scripture and Sunna designate the Imams through the authority and purification verses, the Ark and Two Weighty Things reports, and reports about Uli al-amr transmitted by Shi‘i and Sunni routes.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن ذلك منصوص عليه في الكتاب والسنة كآية الولاية وآية التطهير

rows.speaker: بعض المعترضين
rows.claim: Another objection says obedience is conditional on knowing the Imams, so the unrestricted verse would impose an impossible duty.
rows.anchor: أن طاعتهم مشروطة بمعرفتهم فإنها من دون معرفتهم تكليف بما لا يطاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is a prerequisite to every obligation; identifying the council from ordinary judgment instead of divine instruction does not remove that prerequisite or make the verse less absolute.
rows.anchor: فإن الطاعة مشروطة بالمعرفة مطلقا وإنما الفرق أن أهل الحل والعقد يعرف مصداقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge marks whether an obligation has reached a person and its subject; it is not like ordinary conditions such as pilgrimage capacity or access to water, which would otherwise make every obligation conditional.
rows.anchor: فإنها راجعة إلى تحقق بلوغ التكليف فلا تكليف من غير معرفة به وبموضوعه ومتعلقه

rows.speaker: بعض المعترضين
rows.claim: A third objection says people today cannot reach the infallible Imam to learn religion from him, so he cannot be the one whose obedience God imposed.
rows.anchor: في زماننا هذا عاجزون عن الوصول إلى الإمام المعصوم وتعلم العلم والدين منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community’s inability results from its own wrongdoing and betrayal, not from God or the Messenger; killing a Prophet would not excuse disobedience, and the council alternative is likewise unavailable today.
rows.anchor: ذلك مستند إلى نفس الأمة في سوء فعالها وخيانتها على نفسها لا إلى الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: بعض المعترضين
rows.claim: A fourth objection says that if Uli al-amr were the infallible Imam, the verse would direct disputes to the Imam rather than to God and the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ولو كان المراد من أولي الأمر الإمام المعصوم لوجب أن يقال فإن تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that the response was already given: the commanded return is, by the earlier reasoning, return to the Imam.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن جوابه تقدم فيما مر من البيان والمراد بالرد الرد إلى الإمام بالتقريب الذي تقدم

rows.speaker: بعض المعترضين
rows.claim: A fifth objection says the verse’s dispute clause has no purpose if an infallible Imam prevents division, since it seems to allow disagreement even among the Imams.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية يبين حكم التنازع مع وجود أولي الأمر وطاعة الأمة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute is among believers about Qur’anic and Prophetic rulings, not about the Imam’s authoritative directions in events; where believers cannot derive a ruling, they ask the infallible Imam.
rows.anchor: فإن التنازع المذكور في الآية إنما هو تنازع المؤمنين في أحكام الكتاب والسنة دون أحكام الولاية الصادرة عن الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parallels the Prophet’s contemporaries, who derived rulings where able and asked him where they could not; the return clause applies both when the Messenger is present and when he is absent, so it is not redundant.
rows.anchor: وذلك نظير ما كان لمن يعاصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كانوا يتفقهون فيما يتمكنون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uli al-amr are specific men of the community whose infallibility and obligatory obedience match the Messenger’s; the generic meaning of the term remains distinct from its intended referents, as with “Messenger” and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: المراد بأولي الأمر في الآية رجال من الأمة حكم الواحد منهم في العصمة وافتراض الطاعة حكم الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute clause follows from the preceding exclusive obedience: religious needs are met by obeying God and the Messenger, leaving no need to refer to anyone else and implying that believers must not obey tyranny.
rows.anchor: حيث أوجب طاعة الله ورسوله وهذه الطاعة إنما هي في المواد الدينية التي تتكفل رفع كل اختلاف مفروض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the address is to believers, the dispute is among them, not between them and Uli al-amr or among Uli al-amr, since either alternative conflicts with their required obedience and infallibility.
rows.anchor: وتوجه الخطاب إلى المؤمنين كاشف عن أن المراد بالتنازع هو تنازعهم بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “anything” is broad, referral to God and the Messenger indicates disputes over revealed rulings, not independent commands within the leaders’ authority such as mobilization, war, or peace.
rows.anchor: إذ لا معنى لإيجاب الرد إلى الله والرسول في هذه الموارد مع فرض طاعتهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God and the Messenger may enact or abrogate religious rulings; Uli al-amr and everyone else have no authority to alter what they legislated.
rows.anchor: ليس لأحد أن يتصرف في حكم ديني شرعه الله ورسوله وأولوا الأمر ومن دونهم في ذلك سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “if you believe in God” intensifies the command; violating it stems from corrupted faith and exposes a profession of belief that conceals disbelief, as the following verses indicate.
rows.anchor: فالحكم يرتبط به ارتباطا فالمخالفة تكشف عن التظاهر بصفة الإيمان بالله ورسوله واستبطان للكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ta’wīl means the actual interest from which a ruling arises and which follows from acting on it; the author refers to his discussion at 3:7.
rows.anchor: والتأويل هو المصلحة الواقعية التي تنشأ منها الحكم ثم تترتب على العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann means belief whether or not it matches reality, unlike knowledge, which is belief that does match reality; its frequent use for false belief does not make falsity part of its definition.
rows.anchor: الزعم هو الاعتقاد بكذا سواء طابق الواقع أم لا بخلاف العلم فإنه الاعتقاد المطابق للواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭāghūt is originally a verbal noun like rahabūt, jabarūt, and malakūt, though it can be used as an emphatic agent noun.
rows.anchor: والطاغوت مصدر بمعنى الطغيان كالرهبوت والجبروت والملكوت غير أنه ربما يطلق ويراد به اسم الفاعل مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word first described water overflowing its bounds, then metaphorically described humans exceeding the limits set by reason or religion; usage became literal, including the sense of an oppressor or any object worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: فالطاغوت هو الظالم الجبار والمتمرد عن وظائف عبودية الله استعلاء عليه تعالى وهكذا وإليه يعود ما قيل إن الطاغوت كل معبود من دون الله
